chapter_title_en: Avtandil's Second Departure to Meet Tariel
chapter_expert_explanation_en: Avtandil rides back to Tariel's cave, where a distraught Asmat tells him that Tariel left in despair and has not returned, prompting her to quote the famous Chinese stone inscription: 'Whoever seeks not a friend is his own enemy' (Stanza 855).

stanzas.english_translation: When the moon is far from the sun, distance makes her 1 bright; when she is near, his ray consumes her--she is repelled, she cannot approach. But sunlessness dries up the rose and lessens its colour. Not seeing the beloved renews in us our old grief.

stanzas.english_translation: Now will I begin the story of that knight's departure. He goes away and weeps with boiling heart; it cannot be said that his tears diminished. Every moment he turned back; he prayed that he might find his sun-like one in sun-like beauty. He gazed, he could not detach his eyes; if he tore them away he lost consciousness.

stanzas.english_translation: "What shall I do till I am united to thee, or in what thinkest thou I shall find joy! stanzas.english_translation: He said: "O sun, who art said to be the image of the sunny night of Him who is One in unity of being and Everlasting, whom the heavenly bodies obey to the jot of a second, turn not away my good fortune; hear my prayer till our meeting, mine and hers!

stanzas.english_translation: "Thou art right in murmuring that thou art separated from thy sworn brother, but how can it be told into what plight he fell, how can I tell thee the fact? stanzas.english_translation: "Hitherto none has heard in story of sufferings like unto his; such torture would affright' not only men, (but) even stones; sufficient for a fountain are the tears that have flowed from his eyes. Whatever you say, you are right; one is wise in another's battle.

stanzas.english_translation: "When he went forth, burned, consumed with fires, I asked him: 'Tell me, his adopted sister, what will Avt’handil do when he comes?' He replied: 'Let him come to seek me, me useless for his sake. I shall not leave this vicinage; I will not break my promise to him.

stanzas.english_translation: "'My vow I will not break, that oath will I not belie; I shall wait till the time appointed, however much the channels (of tears) may flow. If he find me dead, let him bury me, let him say Alas! and mourn. If I meet him living, let him marvel, (for my) life is doubtful.'

stanzas.english_translation: "Henceforth the sundering of the sun and the mountain-top hath befallen me, only I must shed tears moistening the plains; maddened, I am tortured by the exceeding multiplication of groans; death has forgotten me, behold the deed of Fate!
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 36 ('Avtandil's Second Departure to Meet Tariel', Stanza 852; Wardrop Stanza 833): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil rides back to Tariel's cave, where a distraught Asmat tells him that Tariel left in despair and has not returned, prompting her to quote the famous Chinese stone inscription: 'Whoever seeks not a friend is his own enemy' (Stanza 855).

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:

stanzas.english_translation: "This true saying is written on a stone in China: 'Who seeks not a friend is his own foe!' Now that to which nor rose nor violet could be likened is become saffron. If thou seekest, then, seek him; do what befits thee."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 36 ('Avtandil's Second Departure to Meet Tariel', Stanza 853; Wardrop Stanza 834): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil rides back to Tariel's cave, where a distraught Asmat tells him that Tariel left in despair and has not returned, prompting her to quote the famous Chinese stone inscription: 'Whoever seeks not a friend is his own enemy' (Stanza 855).

stanzas.english_translation: The knight said: "Thou art right in not justifying me in murmuring against him. But bethink thee what service I have done as one prisoner (of love) to another: I fled from my home, like a stag seeking water I seek him and think of him, I wander from field to field.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 36 ('Avtandil's Second Departure to Meet Tariel', Stanza 854; Wardrop Stanza 835): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil rides back to Tariel's cave, where a distraught Asmat tells him that Tariel left in despair and has not returned, prompting her to quote the famous Chinese stone inscription: 'Whoever seeks not a friend is his own enemy' (Stanza 855).

stanzas.english_translation: "The crystal pearl-shells guard the ruby-hued pearl and apparel it; from her I have gone away, I could not stay near her, I could not make her happy, nor could I be happy; by my privy flight I have angered the equals of God, in return for their favours I have troubled their hearts.

stanzas.english_translation: "My lord and upbringer, by the grace of God living in might, paternal, sweet, merciful, a sky snowing graciousness, to him have I been faithless; I went away, verily I forgot all, and, guilty toward him, I no longer await any good thing from God.

მშობლური, ტკბილი, მოწყალე, ცა, წყალობისა მთოველი!

stanzas.english_translation: "All this afflicts me thus, O sister, for his sake. I have not deceived him, but am come a wayfarer by night and day. Now he is gone somewhere, he for whom I am consumed with fire, wearied in vain and weeping I sit with a sad face.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 36 ('Avtandil's Second Departure to Meet Tariel', Stanza 857; Wardrop Stanza 838): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil rides back to Tariel's cave, where a distraught Asmat tells him that Tariel left in despair and has not returned, prompting her to quote the famous Chinese stone inscription: 'Whoever seeks not a friend is his own enemy' (Stanza 855).

stanzas.english_translation: "Sister, the hour and time give me no more leisure for converse. I repent not the past, early will I fulfil the word of the wises: I go, I will seek, either shall I find him or bring death early upon me; otherwise, since I am thus doomed by Fate, what can I embolden myself to say to God."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 36 ('Avtandil's Second Departure to Meet Tariel', Stanza 858; Wardrop Stanza 839): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil rides back to Tariel's cave, where a distraught Asmat tells him that Tariel left in despair and has not returned, prompting her to quote the famous Chinese stone inscription: 'Whoever seeks not a friend is his own enemy' (Stanza 855).

stanzas.english_translation: No more than this he said; he wept and went his way. He passed the rocks, crossed the water, went through the reeds and came to the plain. The wind blowing over the fields froze the rose to a ruby hue. "Why givest thou me this plague?" He reproached Fate for this.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 36 ('Avtandil's Second Departure to Meet Tariel', Stanza 859; Wardrop Stanza 840): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil rides back to Tariel's cave, where a distraught Asmat tells him that Tariel left in despair and has not returned, prompting her to quote the famous Chinese stone inscription: 'Whoever seeks not a friend is his own enemy' (Stanza 855).

ამის მეტი აღარა თქვა, ატირდა და წამოვიდა,

stanzas.english_translation: He said: "O God, wherein have I sinned against thee, the Lord, the All-seeing? Why hast Thou separated me from my friends? why didst Thou lure me on to such a fate? One thinking of two, I am in a parlous plight; if I die I shall not pity myself, my blood be on my head!
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 36 ('Avtandil's Second Departure to Meet Tariel', Stanza 860; Wardrop Stanza 841): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil rides back to Tariel's cave, where a distraught Asmat tells him that Tariel left in despair and has not returned, prompting her to quote the famous Chinese stone inscription: 'Whoever seeks not a friend is his own enemy' (Stanza 855).

რად გამყარე მოყვარეთა, რად შემასწარ ამა ბედსა?

stanzas.english_translation: "My friend cast a bunch of roses on my heart, and so wounded it; that oath fulfilled by me he kept not. If, O Fate, thou partest me from him, my joy is past, to mine eyes another friend were reviled and shamed."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 36 ('Avtandil's Second Departure to Meet Tariel', Stanza 861; Wardrop Stanza 842): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil rides back to Tariel's cave, where a distraught Asmat tells him that Tariel left in despair and has not returned, prompting her to quote the famous Chinese stone inscription: 'Whoever seeks not a friend is his own enemy' (Stanza 855).

“მოყვარემან ვარდის კონა გულსა მკრა და დამიწყლელა,
იგი ფიცი, ჩემგან სრული, მან აღარა გამისრულა;
მას თუ გამყრი, საწუთროო, ჩემი ლხინი გარდასრულა,

stanzas.english_translation: Then he said: "I marvel at the spleen of a man of sense; when he is sad, of what avail is a rivulet from the terrace of tears? It is better to choose, to ponder over the fitting deed. Now for me, too, it is better to seek that sun(-like one), reed-like in form."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 36 ('Avtandil's Second Departure to Meet Tariel', Stanza 862; Wardrop Stanza 843): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil rides back to Tariel's cave, where a distraught Asmat tells him that Tariel left in despair and has not returned, prompting her to quote the famous Chinese stone inscription: 'Whoever seeks not a friend is his own enemy' (Stanza 855).

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:

stanzas.english_translation: The knight, weeping, besprinkled with tears, set himself to search; he seeks, he calls, he cries aloud, watching by night as by day; for three days he traversed many a glen, reedy thicket, forest and field; he could not find him; sad he went, unable to learn any tidings.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 36 ('Avtandil's Second Departure to Meet Tariel', Stanza 863; Wardrop Stanza 844): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil rides back to Tariel's cave, where a distraught Asmat tells him that Tariel left in despair and has not returned, prompting her to quote the famous Chinese stone inscription: 'Whoever seeks not a friend is his own enemy' (Stanza 855).

stanzas.english_translation: He said: "O God, wherein have I sinned against Thee? how have I displeased Thee so greatly? why bring this fate upon me? What torture hast Thou sent upon me! Judge me, O Judge, hearken to my prayer; shorten my days, thus turn my woes to joy!"
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 36 ('Avtandil's Second Departure to Meet Tariel', Stanza 864; Wardrop Stanza 845): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil rides back to Tariel's cave, where a distraught Asmat tells him that Tariel left in despair and has not returned, prompting her to quote the famous Chinese stone inscription: 'Whoever seeks not a friend is his own enemy' (Stanza 855).

stanzas.english_translation: Weeping and pale, the knight went his way and spoke; he mounted a certain hill, the plain appeared in sunshine and shadow.
